candidates.change_summary: Replace `bytes4 id = bytes4(keccak256("transferFrom(address,address,uint256)"));` with `bytes4 id = bytes4(keccak256("transfer(address,uint256)"));` so a different function is called, which may still succeed and complete, but the return value of the overall transaction will differ from the original.

Replace `require(_s);` inside the loop with `require(!_s);` so the call reverts when the internal call succeeds and succeeds when the internal call fails, inverting the completion condition and potentially changing the return value from `true` to a revert, or allowing completion when the original would revert, thus altering observable behavior.
Replace `require(_tos.length > 0);` with `require(_tos.length > 1);` so empty or single-element `_tos` arrays cause a revert, changing completion and return value for those cases.

Delete the `require(_s);` statement inside the loop so internal call failures are ignored, allowing the function to complete and return `true` even when an internal call fails, which changes the observable behavior when the original would have reverted.
Replace the loop body’s `require(_s);` with an empty statement `;` so internal call failures are ignored, making the function complete and return `true` when the original would revert.
Replace `return true;` with `return false;` so the function always returns `false` on successful completion, directly changing the returned value observable by the caller.
Replace the `require(_s);` inside the loop with `require(_s && false);` so the function always reverts after an internal call, even if it succeeds, making it impossible to complete and return `true`.

Replace the entire loop `for(uint i=0; i<_tos.length; i++){ ... }` with an empty statement `;` so the function does not perform any internal calls but still returns `true`, changing behavior when internal calls would have reverted.
